issue_text:
# REQ-W3: Option 3 runs in a thread

Source: CSE1100 programming exam, 06-11-2024, "Wadden Islands Ferry Company" (`Waddenislands/programming_exam_nov_2024.pdf`, page 4).
The base is the human-written exam solution in `Waddenislands/`; this change was written by an agent.

## Option 3 (existing behaviour)

The total amount of all tickets issued for a certain route (e.g., Texel – Vlieland; a route is
uni-directional, so Vlieland – Texel is a different route!) is calculated and shown on the screen.
The route is requested from the user through the command line. Example output:

    All tickets in the database for the route Terschelling -> Vlieland combined are worth 155 euros.

## Extension (this requirement)

While the current input file is rather small, it can be expected that the database will grow quite
large during the tourist season. Tickets need to stay available while running the Option 3 query.
That is why you should implement Option 3 to make use of threads. Please ensure that Option 3 is
executed in a thread.

## Standards that apply to every change

- At least one unit test per non-trivial method (constructors, getters, setters and methods that
  only read user input or files are exempt); aim for 75% line coverage.
- Nice programming style, checked with CheckStyle (`checkstyle.xml`): method length, number of
  parameters, cyclomatic complexity, Javadoc, line length.
- The menu loops; option 5 stops the program.

findings.title: The worker thread reads ticket data with no synchronization
findings.text: The query thread goes through the ticket list while the main thread can keep changing it through the other menu options, and nothing in Terminal synchronizes access. The issue's goal is for tickets to stay available while the query runs. If a ticket is added during a long query, the result can be a ConcurrentModificationException in the worker or a total that is out of date or inconsistent. With the current small input file the race window is tiny, so it will not show up in practice yet.

confidence.basis: facts backed by C2, C5, C18

findings.title: The result is printed whenever it is ready and can land in the middle of the next prompt
findings.text: Main does not join the thread, so the menu is printed again right away. The turnover line is printed from the worker thread whenever it finishes, which can be in the middle of the menu or another option's input prompts. This is the expected cost of keeping the terminal responsive, but the user sees the result in an unpredictable place. If option 5 is chosen while the query runs, the thread is not a daemon thread, so the result is still printed before the JVM exits.

confidence.basis: facts backed by C1, C4, C19

findings.title: Errors in the worker thread are not handled
findings.text: If the calculation or the callback throws (for example the ConcurrentModificationException from F1), the default handler prints a stack trace on stderr and the user gets no Option 3 message at all.

findings.title: The output format is kept by reusing toStringTurnOver
findings.text: The thread body calls the existing toStringTurnOver, and the new test asserts the exact 155-euro message for Terschelling -> Vlieland. That test also checks that the work ran on a different thread from the caller. The old public method is unchanged.

confidence.basis: facts backed by C8, C9, C11, C12, C13

findings.title: Existing Javadoc calls the route 'omnidirectional', but the issue says routes are one-way
findings.text: The calculateTurnOver Javadoc was already there before this change and says 'omnidirectional', which contradicts the issue. The code behaviour is still tested one-way (Terschelling -> Vlieland). The comment is misleading but was not introduced by this change.

findings.title: Nothing tests the concurrent case or the Main wiring
findings.text: The only test runs the thread with nothing else happening at the same time. No test sells or adds tickets during the query, which is the scenario the requirement is about. No test drives option 3 through Main either.

refusals.question: How consistent should the Option 3 total be when tickets are sold while the query is running?
refusals.why: This decides whether ticket sales may be blocked, or the data copied, while the query runs. That is a trade-off between data correctness and ticket availability, which the issue names as the goal but does not resolve.
refusals.agent_choice: No synchronization. The worker reads the live list while sales continue.
options: Copy the list when the query starts and count the copy
Make ticket access thread-safe (synchronized or a concurrent collection)
Accept the race as-is for this exam scope

refusals.question: Should the menu wait for the Option 3 result or come back right away?
refusals.why: 'Executed in a thread' is met either way. 'Tickets stay available' points to not waiting, but then the output order is unpredictable. The issue does not say which matters more.
refusals.agent_choice: Do not wait. The result is printed whenever the thread finishes.
options: Keep the current behaviour (async, print when done)
Join the thread before showing the menu again
Queue the result and print it at the next menu redraw
